cohort: The study included 152 perimenopausal and postmenopausal women attending gynecological Outpatient Departments in a tertiary hospital.
finding: The overall prevalence of Genitourinary syndrome of menopause (GSM) among perimenopausal and postmenopausal women was 68.4%, with women aged 51-55 years, those who have experienced menopause, women with comorbidities and predisposing gynecological diseases, and those who are obese having a higher risk of developing Vulvovaginal atrophy (VVA).
mod_finding: Mode of delivery at birth did not show a significant association with Vulvovaginal atrophy (VVA).
